resources.string: Fixes the monochrome notification icons that MIUI has broken since version 12.5 by fankes@github

When an app is enabled, its colored notification icons are replaced with the monochrome icons provided in the list.\nThe Override option ignores the app\'s own monochrome icon and always uses the one provided in the list.
Keep this off unless needed. Turn it on only when the module is malfunctioning, then send the debug log to the developer so the problem can be located quickly.
Remove status bar icon count limit

This option is on by default. By default, MIUI shows at most 3 status bar icons (1 on HyperOS) and collapses the rest into an ellipsis. You can set a custom maximum below. Setting it to 0 shows only an ellipsis in place of the icons. The maximum is capped at 100 to avoid errors, and icons that do not fit may be covered by the signal or network speed indicators.

How this works on HyperOS/MIUI depends on your device\'s display cutout. With a centered punch-hole, notification icons never extend past the punch-hole area, however many there are. With a punch-hole on the left or right, they never extend past the signal icons on the right.

This option is on by default. When enabled, the notification icons in the classic (MIUI-style) notification shade also use the replaced icons. Otherwise the icons set by the system are kept. (Not compatible with every system version)

This option is off by default. When enabled, the notification icons in the notification shade ignore their own tint attribute and are all tinted with the system default color (the uniform color provided by the system). This overrides native notification icon behavior and is only provided for users who need it. We do not recommend enabling it, so please decide based on your own preference.

This option is off by default. When enabled, the notification icons in the notification shade are replaced by the app\'s own icon, while the icons in the status bar are not changed. This overrides native notification icon behavior and is only provided for users who need it. We do not recommend enabling it, so please decide based on your own preference.

Later MIUI versions give some notifications a custom colored icon that only system apps can use and third-party apps cannot (this is also a kind of breakage). When this option is enabled and a MIUI custom notification icon is found, it is used first as the replacement (for example: Select Input Method, Fused Location and Bluetooth Headset).
This option is off by default. When an unadapted colored notification icon is found, the status bar shows a built-in placeholder icon instead, and the icon in the notification shade stays unchanged.
Forces color inversion for Focus notifications. Since the inversion cannot be determined accurately, this is a manual override. (Off by default)

This option is on by default. When the notification icon optimization list contains data, newly installed apps are checked for adaptation data automatically, and you are notified if there is none. If you know that the notification icons of the apps you install follow the native monochrome specification, you can turn this reminder off.

Q. How was this module born?

A. This module exists because of MIUI's non-compliant changes. After MIUI 9, the system provided a native notification icon style, but users later reported black and white blocks often appearing in the notification shade.
This is of course not the system's fault, but the result of the extremely non-compliant notification icon design of Chinese apps and Mi Push.
However, after receiving feedback, the MIUI team chose to simply ignore the problem. Starting with the "2021-05-18" development build, all notification icons were changed to the colored app icon, which also broke native icons that used to have their own style.
For Android developers, "setSmallIcon" in the official documentation no longer applies to modified MIUI, which seriously breaks a great many status icons.
Of course, apart from Mi Push marketing notifications, notifications on Chinese phones mostly come from social apps, so most people may not care.
This module was created precisely to fix the icon problem that the MIUI team ignored, and it fixes the black and white block icons on MIUI perfectly.

A. LSPosed is recommended. In its scope, just check \"System UI\". After applying the settings, System UI needs to be restarted. If you installed the \"modern\" variant of the module, on LSPosed 2.1.0+ the module supports hot reload, so later module updates no longer require restarting System UI.
Q. What are the known issues?

A. Known issues:
(1) Animated small icons may flicker on newer systems. This is caused by MIUI forcibly applying the app icon. No solution has been found yet, and forcing a workaround would break native animations. It will be revisited when a solution appears.
(2) Always keep LSPosed up to date, since older versions may fail to apply the hook. If the latest version still does not work, long-press "System UI" in the scope and choose "Deoptimize".
(3) Some users reported that notification icon inversion may fail on early Android 13 beta builds of MIUI 13 and 14. The MIUI team fixed this in the "2022-09-29" development build. If you run into the same problem, update your system to the latest version.
(4) Adapting small icons in the MIUI classic notification style cannot be guaranteed on every supported system version. On some Android 11/12 stable or development builds this function may be buggy and not work. It cannot be investigated or fixed for now, and long-pressing "System UI" and choosing "Deoptimize" does not fix it either. This may be a problem in MIUI itself. If your system has this problem but you still want native-style notification icons, switch the notification style to native in MIUI's "Notification display settings". (Note: modifying the small icons of the MIUI classic style only supports MIUI 12 and later)
(5) Use the module on the MIUI 12.5 "2021-05-18" development build or later. Earlier versions may have MIUI bugs that make the module ineffective or show black and white block icons, and they are no longer supported.
(6) The dynamic System UI refresh may behave differently across system versions. If black and white block icons, display glitches or refresh failures occur, simply restart System UI manually once.
